system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: the system assembles a prompt containing the parent’s source code, performance metrics, identified areas for improvement, and retrieved exemplars
system_prompt_style.note: Prompt rebuilt each generation from parent program plus retrieved inspirations.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: Inspiration retrievalgatherskexemplar programs including the global best, recent top performers, and structurally diverse neighbors from the MAP-Elites grid
env_context_strategy.note: No repository/file-tree context or navigation tools; only the program under evolution and exemplar programs are injected.

observation_format.evidence_quote: The system provides both complete code listings and a metrics comparison table to the LLM

tool_call_format.evidence_quote: In differential mode, the LLM produces diff patches modifying specific code regions... Infull rewrite mode, the LLM generates complete programs from scratch
tool_call_format.note: Model output is code (diff or program), not tool calls.

edit_primitive.evidence_quote: MadEvolve’s ensemble supports three analogous generation modes. In differential mode, the LLM produces diff patches modifying specific code regions
edit_primitive.note: Third mode is synthesis (crossover), also producing full programs. Diff format described for reference systems as SEARCH/REPLACE blocks.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: The central controller orchestrates the evolutionary process through an asynchronous loop coordinating sampling, generation, evaluation, and selection. Each iteration proceeds through six stages.
loop_primitives.note: Population-based evolutionary search: many independent candidate programs scored and selected.

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: Each iteration proceeds through six stages.
planning_granularity.note: The six stages are fixed controller phases; no plan is produced or stored by the LLM.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: Variation generationthen queries the LLM ensemble for code modifications
multi_agent_topology.note: An ensemble of models selected by a bandit, but a single generator role; a separate LLM call writes the report.

delegation_mechanism.note: Model selection only; no agent-to-agent delegation described.

human_in_loop.evidence_quote: The loop continues until reaching a target fitness, exhausting the iteration budget, or detecting stagnation.
human_in_loop.note: Loop is fully automatic; humans consume the generated report afterwards.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: population updateincorporates the program into the database, updating the MAP-Elites grid, island populations, and elite archive

self_verification.evidence_quote: The candidate undergoesfitness evaluationagainst the task-specific protocol.
self_verification.note: Harness-run physics-based evaluator scores every candidate; closest value to automatic execution-based verification.

retry_policy.evidence_quote: The loop continues until reaching a target fitness, exhausting the iteration budget, or detecting stagnation.
retry_policy.note: Repeated generations until target fitness or budget/stagnation.

termination_condition.evidence_quote: The loop continues until reaching a target fitness, exhausting the iteration budget, or detecting stagnation.

cost_controls.evidence_quote: dynamically routing queries to the model that has historically produced the largest fitness improvements, using a UCB1 strategy
cost_controls.note: MadEvolve adopts this bandit-based model selection; base weights reflect cost or capability preferences.

tracing.evidence_quote: Each program in the lineage is stored with its generation number, fitness score, the proposing LLM model name, and the diff that produced it (all recorded in the program metadata).

eval_hooks.evidence_quote: We make MadEvolve and our three tasks publicly available atmadevolve.org.
eval_hooks.note: Task-specific evaluators ship with the framework as the fitness protocol.

target_domain.evidence_quote: We develop a general framework to discover scientific algorithms and apply it to three problems in computational cosmology.

open_source.note: Described as a light-weight open-source framework; licence text not in evidence.

model_agnostic.evidence_quote: fast, lightweight models (e.g., Gemini Flash) maximize throughput by testing many candidates, while larger, more capable models (e.g., GPT-5, Gemini Pro) occasionally propose higher-quality structural innovations

primary_artifact.evidence_quote: MadEvolve: Evolutionary Optimization of Cosmological Algorithms with Large Language Models
primary_artifact.note: Coded from the arXiv paper (2602.15951); the repo URL supplied in the record (A-EVO-Lab/a-evolve) is a different system, A-Evolve.
